title: Work IQ: agents can execute reusable recipes
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap record and the cited documentation supports its general Work IQ controls. Recipe-specific defaults, licensing and configuration remain unconfirmed, and the briefing clearly separates those gaps from documented platform behaviour.

claims.claim: General Work IQ API usage is billed through Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals with appId fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 provisions the organisation's Work IQ service principal.
A dedicated admin-centre navigation path for Work IQ API provisioning is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: enable Work IQ API tenant Microsoft Entra admin center service principal UI. Opened Enable your tenant for Work IQ and Foundry Work IQ setup. The documented admin-center tab uses Graph Explorer to execute the Graph API, not an admin-centre setting path.

claims.claim: App consent is granted in Microsoft Entra admin center under Entra ID > App registrations > app > API permissions > Grant admin consent for [your tenant].
claims.quote: In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com/), go to **Entra ID** > **App registrations** > select the app > **API permissions**. Select **Grant admin consent for [your tenant]**.

claims.claim: Graph grants tenant-wide delegated consent using POST /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants with clientId, consentType AllPrincipals, resourceId and scope, and revokes it using DELETE /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants/{grant-id}.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants
The **consentType** is `AllPrincipals`, indicating that you're consenting on behalf of all users in the tenant.
To revoke all grants, send a DELETE request to the oauth2PermissionGrant object.

claims.claim: WorkIQAgent.Ask is the delegated permission for an application to ask Work IQ.
claims.quote: Register a client application and grant the delegated `WorkIQAgent.Ask` permission.

claims.claim: On the app's API permissions page, select WorkIQAgent.Ask and Revoke admin consent to revoke consent.
claims.quote: On the same **API permissions** page, select the `WorkIQAgent.Ask` permission and select **Revoke admin consent**.

claims.claim: Existing tokens remain valid until expiry after admin consent is revoked.
claims.quote: Existing tokens remain valid until they expire; no new tokens can be issued after revocation.

claims.claim: Graph DELETE removes all permission grants represented by that oauth2PermissionGrant object.
claims.quote: To revoke all grants, send a DELETE request to the oauth2PermissionGrant object.

claims.claim: Tenant Work IQ MCP policy is managed in Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select **Agents** > **Tools**.
In the tools registry, select **Work IQ MCP**.
On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the **Policy** tab when it's available.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for the tenant Work IQ MCP policy toggle is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy automation Microsoft Graph beta API policy settings; "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "graph.microsoft.com/beta". Opened MCP policy governance and checked Graph-targeted results; no method or endpoint for configuring this toggle found.

claims.claim: A recipe-specific tenant control is not documented on either the admin UI or API surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "recipes" "default" "enable"; "Work IQ" "recipes" "controls" "API" "audit". Opened Work IQ overview, API overview, tenant enablement and MCP policy governance; no recipe-specific UI or automation control found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly confirmed how the listed general Work IQ controls apply to recipes.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "recipes" "controls" "API" "audit"; "Work IQ" "recipes" "authoring" "permissions". Opened tenant enablement, Foundry admin management and MCP policy governance; none explicitly places recipes within these control surfaces.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy documentation says mutation operations are disallowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy documentation lets administrators enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: General Work IQ API usage has Copilot Credits spending controls.
